newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar rises after "too loose" warning by RBNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar rises after "too loose" warning by RBNZ.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar rebounded 21 points on the Trade Weighted Index on Thursday within 20 minutes of Reserve Bank governor Don Brash saying monetary conditions had eased too far, in what currency dealers said was a reasonably muted response.
"It is not an excessively large upward movement yet," ANZ's head of foreign exchange Bill Murdoch said shortly after the RBNZ statement when the TWI was up 14 points.
Before the RBNZ announcement at 0100 GMT the TWI was at 66.28, but hit 66.49 before easing back slightly.
The RBNZ's monetary conditions index (MCI) hit a low of 748.48 before Brash's statement, more than 25 points below the lowest point in the band the bank has indicated it would be comfortable with.
"We haven't done as much as the RBNZ would like, I wouldn't imagine," said Bankers Trust New Zealand head of foreign exchange Sean Brown.
"We haven't come back within their band, which I imagine from the RBNZ's point of view will be a little bit frustrating."
ANZ's Murdoch said the RBNZ had given a clear indication of what it wanted, and although it reacted when the MCI was down about 75 points he did not expect them to come in at that point every time.
The bank had said it might tolerate minor breaches of its comfort zone, especially when they were short-lived.
Murdoch said most of the downward pressure on the MCI had come from the soft dollar, and most of the MCI's upward retracement was caused by the dollar's rise.

"Interest rates have been reasonable stable. They have gone up a little bit today, but it has been the downward pressure on the dollar that has been causing the weakness in the MCI, so it has reacted quicker."
He said there had been a lot of selling interest in the market after recent trading house tips to switch out of the kiwi into the Australian dollar.
"There has been a bit of disinvestment out of the NZ dollar over the last 24 hours or so and that is making the retracement in the kiwi-U.S. a little more muted," Murdoch said.
